text:
bankco-sre: Hi team — after migrating our Auth proxy to use the VPCE for Redwood API, auth flows that talk to our internal LDAP (SRV records) started failing with TLS handshake errors. Usuarios hitting API get 502s and our logs show TLS error + certificate subject mismatch. Can help debug?

maya: thanks — can you paste the minimal repro (curl/openssl) and the error lines from our gateway logs? Also which endpoint IP you see resolving inside your VPC?

bankco-sre: repro below. Resolved name is api.redwood.internal -> 10.0.5.12 (this is our VPCE interface IP). From our onprem proxy:

```
# curl (failing when DNS resolves to VPCE ip)
curl -v https://api.redwood.internal/health
* Rebuilt URL to: https://api.redwood.internal/health
*   Trying 10.0.5.12...
* TCP_NODELAY set
* Connected to api.redwood.internal (10.0.5.12) port 443 (#0)
* ALPN, offering h2
* ALPN, offering http/1.1
* TLSv1.3 (OUT), TLS handshake, Client hello (1):
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS handshake, Server hello (2)
* TLSv1.3 (IN), TLS alert, unknown CA (560):
* SSL: certificate subject name 'api.redwood.net' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.internal'
* Closing connection 0
curl: (51) SSL: certificate subject name 'api.redwood.net' does not match target host name 'api.redwood.internal'
```

bankco-sre: and openssl shows server cert CN=api.redwood.net. We think our proxy is sending SNI as api.redwood.internal (internal SRV), causing mismatch.

ben: yep this smells like SNI vs split-horizon DNS. Private endpoint IP is correct but cert is for the public hostname. When clients use the internal name as the TLS servername, the server presents cert for the public name and the client fails. AWS PrivateLink does TCP pass-through — it doesn't rewrite SNI.

sam: can you try forcing SNI to the public hostname? quick test:

```
# simulate client where DNS points at the VPCE but SNI is public name
curl -v --resolve "api.redwood.net:443:10.0.5.12" -H "Host: api.redwood.net" https://api.redwood.net/health
```

sam: if that succeeds, it's definitely SNI mismatch. Also try with openssl s_client: `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.net` and inspect the cert.

bankco-sre: ran both — with --resolve it returns 200. openssl s_client with -servername returns cert CN=api.redwood.net. Without -servername it returns the same handshake error we saw.

eli: next check: does your onprem proxy rewrite SNI or pick servername from original Host header? Many proxies use the upstream hostname unless configured. If the proxy is using the SRV target (api.redwood.internal) as upstream host, it will send that as SNI.

bankco-sre: our proxy (haproxy) is upstreaming to the SRV CNAME and we didn't set sni or send-proxy options.

maya: two options: short-term workaround and long-term fix. Short-term: configure proxy to set SNI/Server Name to api.redwood.net when proxying to the VPCE IP (haproxy has `sni` directive or `ssl_fc_sni`/`ssl_fc_sni` mapping). For curl testing you can use --resolve. Long-term: ensure your split-horizon DNS returns the public hostname to clients or configure the PrivateLink to accept the internal name (requires cert changes on our side, which is less likely).

ben: also confirm security groups/NACLs allow established ephemeral port ranges back to your proxy and that there is no TLS terminating device in between (WAF/firewall doing TLS-inspect and re-signing). Packet capture helps.

eli: please capture a short pcap on your proxy while reproducing: `sudo tcpdump -i eth0 -w /tmp/redwood-vpce.pcap host 10.0.5.12 and port 443` and share. If you can't share pcap, paste `openssl s_client -connect 10.0.5.12:443 -servername api.redwood.internal -showcerts` and the error text.

bankco-sre: attaching openssl outputs (sanitized). Confirmed SNI differs. We'll change haproxy to set SNI to api.redwood.net and try.

ops-bot: Created escalation ticket INF-2314 and assigned to infra oncall. :rotating_light:

bankco-sre: update — set `req.ssl_sni hdr(host)` -> forced to api.redwood.net in haproxy; tests pass (200) and upstream auth to LDAP completes. Rolling to prod now. Thanks for the quick help! :tada:

maya: great — can you paste the haproxy snippet you used for our KB? Others will hit this.

bankco-sre: sure — snippet below:

```
backend redwood_vpce
  server redwood-1 10.0.5.12:443 ssl verify none sni str(api.redwood.net)
```

maya: perfect — adding to our docs: note about VPCE + split-horizon + SNI mismatch and recommended haproxy/nginx config. Closing once you confirm prod is green.

bankco-sre: prod is green, metrics back to normal. Closing. Thanks again everyone.
